intent: The intent of this schedule is to permit mixed-use residential buildings where all dwelling units are secured as residential rental tenure. In the RR-3A district, developments are permitted up to 4 storeys. In the RR-3B district, developments are permitted up to 6 storeys if a minimum of 20% of the residential floor area is secured as below-market rental dwelling units. In the RR-3C district, developments are permitted up to 6 storeys. [...] For the purposes of this schedule, below-market rental dwelling units has the meaning set out in Schedule J: Affordable Housing Schedule. [...] Without limitation, applicable Council policies and guidelines for consideration include the Residential Rental Districts Schedules Design Guidelines.

clauses.text: The intent of this schedule is to permit mixed-use residential buildings where all dwelling units are secured as residential rental tenure. In the RR-3A district, developments are permitted up to 4 storeys. In the RR-3B district, developments are permitted up to 6 storeys if a minimum of 20% of the residential floor area is secured as below-market rental dwelling units. In the RR-3C district, developments are permitted up to 6 storeys. [...] For the purposes of this schedule, below-market rental dwelling units has the meaning set out in Schedule J: Affordable Housing Schedule. [...] Without limitation, applicable Council policies and guidelines for consideration include the Residential Rental Districts Schedules Design Guidelines.

The table below provides an overview of outright and conditional approval uses in the RR-3A, RR-3B and RR-3C districts, categorized by the minimum site area required, where applicable. Applicable density, form and placement regulations in section 3 of this schedule are cross-referenced in the third column.

All outright and conditional approval uses are subject to all other provisions of this by-law, including Section 2, Section 10 and Section 11, and compliance with the regulations of this schedule including section 2.2. [...] The uses identified in the table below as outright approval uses are permitted in these districts and will be issued a permit. [...] The uses identified in the table below as conditional approval uses may be approved in these districts by the Director of Planning or Development Permit Board, with or without conditions, if the Director of Planning or Development Permit Board considers: [...] Uses are listed under their general land use category. Applicable use-specific regulations in section 2.2 of this schedule are cross-referenced in the third column. Cross-references to applicable use-specific regulations are provided for information purposes only and do not form part of this by-law.
the intent of this schedule and all applicable Council policies and guidelines; and
the submission of any advisory group, property owner or tenant.
Non-dwelling uses listed in section 2.1 of this schedule may be permitted only in a mixed-use residential building.
Mixed-use residential building may include any non-dwelling use listed in section 2.1 of this schedule.

In a mixed-use residential building, dwelling uses are not permitted within a depth of 10.7 m from the front wall of the first storey of a building, extending across the full width of the building, except for entrances to the portion containing dwelling uses.
In the RR-3A district, the second storey and above, measured from the front property line, is limited to dwelling uses only.
In the RR-3B and RR-3C districts, the third storey and above, measured from the front property line, is limited to dwelling uses only.

Any other use that is not specifically listed and defined as a use in Section 2 of this by-law may be permitted as a conditional approval use if the Director of Planning considers the use to be comparable in nature to the uses listed in this schedule, having regard to the intent of this schedule. [...] This section contains density, form and placement regulations organized by use.
All uses in these districts are subject to the following regulations.
For the RR-3B district:
a minimum of 20% of the residential floor area must be secured as below-market rental dwelling units; and
the below-market rental dwelling units are subject to Schedule J: Affordable Housing Schedule.
All dwelling units must be secured as residential rental tenure.
The maximum floor space ratio is: [...] provided that the floor space ratio for non-dwelling uses is at least 0.35.

The maximum height of a building is measured from a plane formed by lines extending horizontally back from the officially established building grades at the front property line.

Despite the maximum building height in sections 3.1.2.2 and 3.1.2.8 above, portions of a building located within 6.1 m of the ultimate rear property line must not exceed 6.1 m in building height measured from base surface, except for portions of a building where the rear yard may be decreased under section 3.1.2.14 below.
The Director of Planning may increase the maximum building height if the Director of Planning considers the intent of this schedule and all applicable Council policies and guidelines.

Despite the minimum side yard width in section 3.1.2.4 above, in the case of a corner site, the front yard regulations in section 3.1.2.3 above and section 3.1.2.17(b) below, apply to the exterior side yard.
The Director of Planning may decrease the minimum side yard width if the Director of Planning considers the intent of this schedule and all applicable Council policies and guidelines.

Despite the minimum rear yard depth in section 3.1.2.5 above, in the case of a corner site where the rear of the site adjoins with the side yard of a site located in an R district, without the intervention of a lane, the minimum depth of the rear yard must be 3.1 m.

Despite the minimum rear setback in section 3.1.2.6 above, in the case of a corner site, for portions of a building above 6.1 m in height, the rear setback may be decreased to a minimum depth of 4.6 m if the portion of the building for which the rear setback is decreased:
is located a minimum distance of 15.3 m from an adjoining site; and
does not exceed 22.8 m in width.
Despite the minimum rear setback in section 3.1.2.6(b) above, roof decks may project into the setback.
The Director of Planning may decrease the minimum rear yard depth or rear setback if the Director of Planning considers the intent of this schedule and all applicable Council policies and guidelines.
If the Director of Planning considers the intent of this schedule and all applicable Council policies and guidelines, the Director of Planning may vary: [...] [Reserved]
the minimum site area;
the minimum front yard depth; and
the minimum setback of exterior walls.
